areas.name: Capacity and throughput
cells: servers needed for a peak requests per second given per-server capacity and a headroom percentage
requests per second from daily active users, actions per user per day and a peak-to-average factor
concurrent connections or threads from an arrival rate and a service time (Little's law)
CPU cores needed for a target queries per second and CPU milliseconds per request
worker pool size for a job arrival rate and job duration at a target utilisation
instances needed to survive the loss of N nodes while staying under a utilisation target
batch job throughput: items per hour from workers and seconds per item, and time to finish a backlog
autoscaling: instances needed to keep a per-instance metric at its target
read and write split: reads per second reaching the primary versus the replicas
connection pool size needed for a query rate and average query time

areas.name: Latency and queueing
cells: end-to-end latency budget across sequential service calls with a known per-call time
probability that all of N parallel calls finish under their p99 (tail amplification from fan-out)
mean queueing delay at a given utilisation for a single server (M/M/1)
worst-case total latency with timeouts and N retries
throughput achievable from latency per request and number of concurrent requests
average latency of a cached read path from hit rate, cache latency and database latency
number of sequential network round trips needed for a connection setup and total time at a given RTT
how much a slower dependency adds to the median or average latency when it is called a fraction of the time

areas.name: Storage and data growth
cells: storage for N records of a given size over a retention period
raw storage needed with a replication factor and filesystem overhead
index or metadata overhead added as a percentage to base data size
backup storage with a daily change rate and a number of retained snapshots
log volume per day from lines per second, bytes per line and a compression ratio
time until a disk fills at a given ingest rate
erasure coding: raw storage for k data and m parity chunks and how many failures it survives
months until a growing database reaches a size limit given monthly growth percent

areas.name: Reliability and availability
cells: allowed downtime per month or year for an availability target
availability of components in series and in parallel
error budget remaining after incidents of known duration
total waiting time for retries with exponential backoff before giving up
expected number of attempts until success given a failure rate
availability from MTBF and MTTR
number of replicas needed so that the chance all fail stays under a target
requests lost during a failover of a known duration at a request rate

areas.name: Caching and cost
cells: cache memory needed for N keys of a given size plus per-key overhead
backend load after raising the cache hit rate from one value to another
dollars saved per month by cache hits on a paid API or database call
requests per second reaching the origin from TTL expiry across many keys
whether a working set fits in a cache of a given size and the resulting hit rate estimate
CDN offload percentage and the egress cost it saves
origin load when a hot key expires and many clients refetch at once

areas.name: Scaling and sharding
cells: number of shards needed for a data size and per-shard capacity with headroom
time to rebalance by moving a share of data at a given transfer rate
write fan-out per post for a follower count and the resulting writes per second
partition count needed for a target throughput and per-partition throughput
load on the busiest shard given a skew factor
data lost in seconds and in records from replication lag at a write rate
fraction of keys moved when adding a node with consistent hashing

areas.name: Cloud cost and planning
cells: monthly bill from instance count, hourly price and hours
months until reserved pricing beats on-demand
egress and storage cost for a monthly data volume with tiered prices
cost per thousand requests from total cost and request volume
monthly savings from moving to smaller instances
spot instance savings with an interruption overhead percentage
months until building in-house pays off against a monthly vendor fee

areas.name: Network and bandwidth
cells: transfer time of a file at a given bandwidth with protocol overhead
bandwidth needed to sustain a data rate with headroom
bandwidth-delay product and the window size needed to fill a link
bandwidth for serving a number of concurrent streams at a bitrate
packets per second at a given bitrate and packet size
time to replicate a dataset across regions over a link at a utilisation cap

areas.name: ML and inference
cells: tokens per second per GPU and GPUs needed for a request rate
KV cache memory from layers, hidden size, precision and context length
model memory from parameter count and bytes per parameter
batch size against per-request latency at a given throughput
cost per million tokens from GPU hourly price and throughput
training or fine-tuning time from tokens, throughput and epochs

areas.name: Other professional
cells: project schedule with team size, parallelism and overhead
monthly loan payment or months to pay a loan off
savings growth with regular deposits and an interest rate
hourly rate needed to take home a target after tax and unbillable time
energy and battery runtime from capacity and power draw
break-even units from fixed cost, price and unit cost

styles: chatty and polite, a full sentence or two
jargon-heavy, a senior engineer in a hurry
a junior engineer who is unsure of the terms
gives a line of context about the project before asking
mixes units (GB and MB, ms and s, per day and per hour)
phrased as a what-if ("if we double...")
asking for a quick estimate for a design review
decline_themes: which technology to choose (a database, a queue, a framework)
explain a concept (CAP theorem, consensus, eventual consistency)
write or fix a config, a query or a snippet of code
an opinion on whether an architecture is a good idea
how to debug a specific symptom with no numbers to compute
a definition or a comparison of two terms
twists: the time is given in seconds or milliseconds per item but the rate is per minute or per hour, so the units must be lined up before the answer
sizes are given in a mix of MB, GB and TB (binary, 1024) and the answer is asked in a different one of those
a count given in millions or billions (for example tokens, rows or parameters) that has to be scaled before use
two percentages that each apply to the same base (for example 18% extra and 4% extra on top of the base), not one after the other
tiered pricing: the first part of the usage costs one price and everything above a threshold costs another
bandwidth in Mbps or Gbps against a size in bytes, so bits and bytes must be converted (use decimal for the link rate)
the answer is a whole number of machines, shards or workers, so it must round up, and a spare or redundant unit is added on top
a daily or hourly total that must be turned into a per-second rate before using a per-second capacity
how long until something fills or finishes, with the inflow and the outflow given in different time units
a one-off cost against a monthly saving or running cost, asking for the number of months to break even
concurrent connections or items in flight from an arrival rate and a time each one stays (Little's law), with the time in milliseconds
an amount per request, per hour or per GB that has to be scaled up to a month of 30 days
